molecular identification of the components of a coculture by DGGE of 16S rDNA fragments can be used to design selective culture conditions that allow the separation and isolation of both components in pure culture.
molecular information on the bacterial composition of cocultures can be used for the identification of components of the mixture and for their subsequent isolation in pure culture.

(i) molecular information about the bacterial species present in a coculture capable to reduce sulfate after exposure to oxi- and microoxic conditions allowed the identification of two different bacteria and (ii) this information was used to isolate the bacteria in pure culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new strategy for the isolation of pure bacterial cultures, which is based on molecular information about the composition of mixed bacterial communities.
the molecular identification of bacteria and their physiological characterization in pure culture.
the molecular analysis of microbial diversity and its application to microbial physiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
molecular identification of the bacterial components of a mixed culture can be a valuable tool for subsequent isolation and characterization in pure culture.
molecular analysis can be used to identify bacteria from a cocultured sample.

molecular identification of the bacteria present in a coculture, by denaturing gradient electrophoresis and sequencing of 16S rRNA genes, can be successfully used as a tool for the isolation of the bacteria in pure culture.

molecular information about the microbial composition of a mixed culture can be used to design specific growth conditions to isolate and study the individual components of the mixture.
